prompt: Create ONE GIANT MASTER PIXEL-ART SPRITE SHEET for the real dog Cooper, using every supplied Cooper reference plus the two supplied photos of his actual green tubular puffy toy/collar object. This is a provisional source canvas for later extraction, not three independent images and not a presentation board. Preserve Cooper: black, grey, and warm cream shaggy Cavoodle coat, cream muzzle and paws, floppy ears, anxious expressive face, curled tail, and the actual object as a dark green fabric-covered puffy tubular loop with repeating white swirl pattern. It must read as a chunky soft tubular accessory/toy, not a flat bandana, neckerchief, ordinary collar, or generic green scarf. Compose one large clean canvas with three clearly separated pixel-art regions: LEFT portrait region, TOP-RIGHT battle region, BOTTOM-RIGHT overworld region. Portrait region: 12 consistent bust cells with neutral, gentle, worried, shocked, sad, determined, defiant, angry, relieved, proud, brave, and helpless-but-resolute expressions. Battle region: 12 consistent full-body RPG battle cells, with many clearly standing or seated upright on TWO LEGS, including upright guard, seated guard, bite/gnaw, leash or tubular loop used as a lasso, playful toy sword-like prop, toy knuckle-duster prop, wind-up, follow-through, hit, stagger, victory, and exhausted standing poses. Do not make every battle cell quadrupedal. Overworld region: strict 4 by 4 grid, rows north/back, south/front, east/right, west/left, four movement phases per row; low top-down orthographic quadruped. All cells must keep Cooper’s face, markings, proportions, accessory, and colour identity consistent across the whole canvas. Use hard-edged discrete square pixel clusters, limited warm late-SNES palette, crisp nearest-neighbour-like edges, no antialiasing, no blur, no photorealism, no painterly gradients, no text, no labels, no UI, no scenery, no decorative framing. Pixel art must be visible at native inspection scale. Treat this as a giant extraction source sheet with logical cells and generous spacing, not a polished illustration.
